title: Food web complexity underlies biodiversity effects on ecosystem functioning.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the Zenodo archive (record 20130985, CC-BY-4.0, 42.5 MB zip, GitHub release ecodivlab/BEF-in-Food-Webs v1.1.1). Opened 'Master dataset_FuSED.csv': 318 rows x 23 columns, 0% missing, ecosystem types Marine 131 / Streams 74 / Soils 65 / Lakes 48, 12 study_IDs (Intertidal rockpools alone has 124). Read 'Barnes et al Metadata.xlsx' (all 23 columns documented, but no units given for flux columns). Counted 320 adjacency matrices and 323 taxon-attribute files: 16,272 nodes and 158,614 feeding links in total. Read the R scripts: fluxes are computed with fluxweb::fluxing() from the adjacency matrix, biomass, body mass, losses and efficiencies.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was available (paywalled, no PMCID). The 318-web count matches the abstract; how the feeding links were compiled (observed gut contents versus literature or feeding rules) was not checked.

a1_downloadable.note: Open Zenodo record, CC-BY-4.0, 42.5 MB zip; downloaded and unzipped without login (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The food-web-level outcomes (flux, prim.consumption, second.consumption, PC.predation) are columns in the master CSV (checked).

a3_inputs_present.note: Per-web adjacency matrices and taxon attribute tables (biomass, body mass, metabolic type) are present as CSVs (checked).

a4_units_stated.note: The metadata sheet describes every column but gives no units for the flux columns; some attribute files have a units column (e.g. 'dry g.m2'), but it is not uniform across the 9 source folders (checked).

a5_enough_rows.note: The modelling unit is the food web: 318 rows, and 124 of them come from one rockpool study (checked). That is far under the ~1,500-row threshold for regression.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 318 food webs in the CSV match the abstract's 318.

a8_label_provenance.note: The energy fluxes are not measured. They come out of a metabolic-theory model (fluxweb's fluxing function) whose inputs are the adjacency matrix, biomass, body mass and metabolic type, so predicting them from food-web features would just relearn that formula (checked in the R scripts).

backbone.name: none: tabular food-web summaries; no pretrained backbone fits

integration.partner_dataset: GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions), a database of species interactions, joined on taxon names (would need name resolution)
integration.join_key: free-text taxon names; no taxonomy IDs in the files
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not pursued because Part A failed.

honest_claim_h3: A model would only claim to reproduce fluxweb's energy-flux formula across 318 food webs from 12 studies, not to predict any measured ecosystem function.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a food web's species count, biomasses and feeding links to predict how much energy flows through it.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per food web: species richness, maximum trophic level, trophic similarity, temperature and a productivity proxy; 318 webs (verified).
plain_idea.predict: Total and per-function energy flux. These are computed by a metabolic-theory model from the same biomass, body-mass and feeding-link data, not measured in the field.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Ecologists could estimate ecosystem function without building full food webs. But the target is a deterministic calculation, so the model would learn a formula, not anything new about ecology.

label_elsewhere.sources: None searched; the fluxes exist only as this paper's derived values for its 318 webs.
label_elsewhere.why: Not applicable: rejected at Part A.

ml_idea: Considered: regress food-web energy flux on richness and structure, holding out whole studies. Also considered: predicting feeding links across 16,272 nodes and 158,614 links, but the provenance of those links (observed versus rule-based) and prior link-prediction work were not checked.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 97 KB master table; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done: the flux labels are fluxweb outputs computed from the input features, and there are only 318 rows.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 and A8. There are only 318 food-web rows, 124 of them from one study, and the energy-flux labels are computed by the fluxweb metabolic model from the same biomass, body-mass and link features, so any predictor would be learning that formula. A4 is also weak: the flux columns have no units. Existing-model search was skipped after the Part A failure.
